summary: Deforms faces and surfaces by pulling target points or isoparametric curves directly on primitive contours instead of editing CVs directly.

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Warp method: matrix, vector, point, or primitive target mode

key_params.name: t
key_params.note: Translation applied by the Clay transform

key_params.name: r

key_params.name: s
key_params.note: Scale applied by the Clay transform

common_gotchas: Clay partially deforms primitives, while Align translates or rotates whole primitives.
Clay does not refine faces or surfaces automatically; add Refine SOP detail around the target for more local control.
With a second input, the destination primitive is the first primitive in that input; without one, primitives snap to themselves.
Faces do nothing when U deform is off, while V deform does not affect face primitives.
Sharpness jumps to valid discrete knot insertion positions on NURBS surfaces.
key_concepts: Clay SOP deforms faces and surfaces by pulling points on primitive contours instead of directly editing CVs.
Matrix, vector, point, and primitive modes define different target deformation workflows.
U and V warp controls act in parametric surface space and have different effects on faces versus surfaces.
Sharpness and bias controls can insert knots or localize deformation but may jump to valid discrete positions.
